pr_title: libnetwork: just forward the external DNS response
pr_body:
- Fixes #45553
- Fixes #45555

<!--
Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines;
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

** Make sure all your commits include a signature generated with `git commit -s` **

For additional information on our contributing process, read our contributing
guide https://docs.docker.com/opensource/code/

If this is a bug fix, make sure your description includes "fixes #xxxx", or
"closes #xxxx"

Please provide the following information:
-->

Changes to the DNS resolver in #44664 fixed some bugs, including load-bearing bugs which masked other bugs. One bug not fixed by the aforementioned PR is that the resolver handles non-authoritative NXDOMAIN responses by failing over to the next external DNS server in the list. That behaviour does not make sense as authoritative responses only come from the authoritative name servers for a domain, and most of the time none of the servers in the list will be authoritative. What would make sense for handling a non-authoritative NXDOMAIN is to recursively resolve up to the authoritative name servers to get an authoritative answer to cache. But our DNS resolver is [a stub resolver, not a recursive resolver,](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8499#section-6) so there is no good reason for it to treat any NXDOMAIN response differently from a NOERROR response. (If you depended on this fail-over behaviour to successfully resolve domains because the first external DNS server in your list returns NXDOMAIN for the public internet, that DNS server is broken and needs to be fixed. If we can make a split-horizon DNS resolver which resolves public domain names by forwarding, so can you.)

Commit 9cf8c4f68955457f15288701eb59da045349b214 fixed a bug in the fail-over behaviour by replying SERVFAIL if none of the external name servers provided a successful response instead of falling through to forward the last non-successful response received. Unfortunately that was a load-bearing bug which masked the aforementioned NXDOMAIN issue.

**- What I did**
Our resolver is just a forwarder for external DNS—a stub resolver—so it should act like it. Unless it's a server failure or refusal, take the response at face value and forward it along to the client. RFC 8020 is only applicable to caching recursive name servers and our resolver is neither caching nor recursive.

**- How I did it**
Deleted code which had no business existing in a DNS stub resolver.

**- How to verify it**
```console
$ docker network create mybridge
$ docker run --rm -t --network mybridge --dns 8.8.8.8 alpine sh -c 'apk add -qU bind-tools && dig nxdomain.test'
```

v24.0.0:

```
;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available
```


issue_context.title: In K8s + dind, DNS forwards SERVFAIL instead of NXDOMAIN
issue_context.body:
### Description

In a K8s cluster (GKE in my case) and Docker-in-Docker (dind) user-defined network, attempting to resolve non-existent domains will result in a `SERVFAIL` instead of a `NXDOMAIN`. This causes DNS clients like c-ares (used by default in gRPC clients) to error out instead of moving on to the next domain in the search path in `etc/resolv.conf`.

This is a bigger problem when attempting to reach other containers by name in a Docker user-defined bridge. If `ndots` is not 0 (5 is the default in GKE iirc) then attempting to resolve a name like `test` will immediately fail with `SERVFAIL` instead of trying all search paths till `test.` is finally attempted and resolved.

From Docker daemon logs, it seems that `NXDOMAIN` was received but when attempting to forward it, the client instead receivs a `SERVFAIL`.

- Likely related to the change in https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/44575 / https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/44664

### Reproduce

1. SSH into a K8s cluster (in my case, GKE)
2. Create a Docker network: `docker network create some-network`
3. Start dind with debug mode: `docker run --privileged --name some-docker -d --network some-network --network-alias docker -e DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR=/certs -v some-docker-certs-ca:/certs/ca -v some-docker-certs-client:/certs/client docker:dind --debug --log-level debug`
4. Connect to dind: `docker run --rm -it --network some-network -e DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR=/certs -v some-docker-certs-client:/certs/client:ro docker:latest sh`
5. Create another network: `docker network create another-network`
6. Run any container here: `docker run --rm -it --network another-network busybox`
7. `nslookup -debug test.test`
8. Get `SERVFAIL` instead of `NXDOMAIN`

```
bash-5.1# dig test.test

; <<>> DiG 9.16.22 <<>> test.test
;; global options: +cmd
;; Got answer:
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 2193
;; flags: qr rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 0
;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available

;; QUESTION SECTION:
;test.test.			IN	A

;; Query time: 3 msec
;; SERVER: 127.0.0.11#53(127.0.0.11)
;; WHEN: Thu May 18 01:24:36 UTC 2023
;; MSG SIZE  rcvd: 27
```

Contents of `/etc/resolv.conf`:
```
search us-central1-c.c.gke-cluster-name.internal c.gke-cluster-name.internal google.internal
nameserver 127.0.0.11
options ndots:0
```

Docker daemon logs:
```
time="2023-05-18T01:24:36.702466753Z" level=debug msg="Name To resolve: test.test."
time="2023-05-18T01:24:36.702639405Z" level=debug msg="[resolver] forwarding query" client-addr="udp:127.0.0.1:44101" dns-server="udp:127.0.0.11:53" question=";test.test.\tIN\t A"
time="2023-05-18T01:24:36.704423670Z" level=debug msg="[resolver] external DNS udp:127.0.0.11 responded with NXDOMAIN for \"test.test.\""
time="2023-05-18T01:24:54.503033244Z" level=debug msg="event forwarded" ns=moby topic=/tasks/exit type=containerd.events.TaskExit
```

### Expected behavior

`NXDOMAIN` so that DNS clients move on to the next suffix in the search path

### Additional Info

#### Workarounds
* If using gRPC, disable the c-ares client by setting `GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER=native`. I don't yet understand why using OS native DNS client works, but not c-ares, when querying the Docker embedded DNS server.
* Always prepend `.` when referring to another container on the same Docker (non-default) bridge network, e.g. `postgres.:5432` rather than `postgres:5432`
comments: We're facing the same issue (on GKE)

I'm hitting the same issue too. Especially, all versions of `Alpine` (based on musl libc) stops iterating searches when it receives `SERVFAIL` , this becomes a big problem that all of the DNS query fails.
Other distributions like Debian, Fedora etc. (based on glibc) continues resolving FQDN even if they hit `SERVFAIL`, they can resolve DNS.
Thank you for the very quick fix!

review_comments:
Still somewhat on the fence on this, as this would be a breaking change (even if the "split horizon" scenario is wrong?). 

TBH part of https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1035#page-27 is a bit ambiguous (or at least, I have no idea how it should be interpreted) (what does "meaningful only" mean? Should be ignored otherwise?);

```
3               Name Error - Meaningful only for
                responses from an authoritative name
                server, this code signifies that the
                domain name referenced in the query does
                not exist.
```

As far as I can tell, "meaningful" is in reference to recursive DNS resolvers, as in a recursive resolver should treat non-authoritative NXDOMAIN responses as a signal to continue recursing to the authoritative name server to get an authoritative response. We are a stub resolver, not a recursive resolver, so our duty is to faithfully return the response provided by the recursive resolver we delegated the handling of the query onto.
